narrative_purpose: Anchors the cold open: midday on Pandora as the giant planet slides across the sun and the land drops into twilight, the sky-fact that tells you you are standing on a moon.
subject: Looking steeply upward from inside an alien forest clearing toward a huge banded gas giant whose dark edge is sliding across a small brilliant white-gold star, partly covering it so a bright ring of light flares around the planet's rim. Tall glowing blue-green canopy trees frame the edges of the upward view.
scene: The moment of a daily eclipse at midday: light on the forest going long, thin and blue as the star is swallowed. Faint banded detail visible on the lit crescent of the giant planet; the rest of its disc in deep shadow.
camera: Steep upward worm's-eye view through a gap in the forest canopy toward the sky.
light: Dramatic backlight from the eclipsed star flaring around the planet's edge; the forest below lit mostly by its own cool bioluminescence as daylight fails.
palette: Void-indigo and deep teal sky, a scarce warm-amber ring of starlight around the dark planet, cyan and living-teal glow on the framing canopy.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, atmospheric, high dynamic range between the bright ring and the dark sky.
detail_level: Crisp on the canopy edges and the bright flaring ring; the planet's shadowed disc smooth and dark.
composition: Planet-and-star high and central; dark forest silhouette framing the lower corners; strong vertical sense of looking straight up.
consistency_notes: Same banded gas giant Polyphemus as the cover (cream/rust/grey bands). Cool Pandora palette, bioluminescent forest key light.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no oversaturation, no cartoon or anime style
